hints: Focus on what lowering the pH really means, it means the solution becomes more acidic with more $\text{H}^+$ ions.
Recall that ammonia forms a basic solution in water, while sulfur dioxide and nitrogen dioxide are acidic non-metal oxides.
Check which two gases form acids on dissolving and which one forms an alkali, then pick the combination with only the acid-formers.
walkthrough:
**What does lowering pH mean?**

Pure water has pH 7. Lowering pH means making $\text{H}^+$ concentration higher, so we are looking for gases that form acidic solutions.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{acidic gas + water} \rightarrow \text{acidic solution (pH < 7)}$$

**Test gas 1, ammonia**

Ammonia is a familiar base. It reacts reversibly with water to make hydroxide ions, so pH goes up, not down.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{NH}_4^+ + \text{OH}^-$$

**Test gas 2, sulfur dioxide**

Sulfur dioxide is an acidic oxide. It dissolves to form sulfurous acid, which releases $\text{H}^+$ and lowers pH. This is one cause of acid rain.

Chemical equation:
$$\text{SO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$$

**Test gas 3, nitrogen dioxide**

Nitrogen dioxide is also acidic. With water it forms a mixture of nitrous acid and strong nitric acid, so $\text{H}^+$ increases and pH falls sharply.

Chemical equation:
$$2\text{NO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{HNO}_2 + \text{HNO}_3$$

**Combine the conclusion**

Only 2 and 3 lower the pH. Statement 1 raises the pH. So the correct combination is 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 all lower pH. Ammonia (1) does the opposite, it produces $\text{OH}^-$ ions and raises pH to above 7, so it cannot be included.
options.B: Incorrect. This would mean 1 and 2 only. While sulfur dioxide (2) is correct, ammonia (1) is basic and raises pH, and nitrogen dioxide (3) is missed even though it strongly acidifies water.
options.C: Correct. Both sulfur dioxide (2) forming $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_3$ and nitrogen dioxide (3) forming $\text{HNO}_2$ and $\text{HNO}_3$ release $\text{H}^+$ ions and lower pH. Ammonia (1) is excluded because it is basic.
options.D: Incorrect. This would mean 1 only. Ammonia alone in water gives $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$, a weak alkali with pH greater than 7, so it raises pH rather than lowering it.
